key_insight: Extract Q-values directly from a behavior-cloned policy and use those Q-estimates to gate online RL updates, so robots can safely and efficiently improve after demonstrations without overwriting previously good behaviors.
problem_solved: Behavior cloning lacks a built-in way to continue improving online and offline-to-online RL can overwrite good demonstrated actions due to distribution mismatch; this work prevents regression while enabling on-robot reinforcement learning.
method: Q-Estimation from BC: derive or infer action-value (Q) estimates from a trained behavior-cloned model to quantify the value of demonstrated actions.
Q-Gating: use the extracted Q-values to decide when to accept online RL updates versus retain the BC action (protecting high-value demonstrated behavior).
Integrate into offline-to-online pipeline for on-robot learning so policy improvements are allowed only where Q-gating signals safe, higher-value alternatives.
impact: Provides a practical, low-risk way to continue improving robot policies after demonstration data is collected, reducing real-world trial-and-error and preventing degradation of demonstrated skills. Useful for practitioners deploying robots that must learn safely and autonomously from limited online interaction.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Demonstrations -> Behavior Cloning -> Q Extraction -> Q-Gating -> Online RL updates (highlight gate decisions).
Before/After bar chart: performance or success-rate showing preserved demo behavior vs improved behavior after Q2RL.
Decision heatmap or toy state-action plot: color-coded Q-values from BC showing where RL is allowed or blocked.
Robot icon with safety shield and progress arrow: communicates safe, incremental improvement on-robot.
paper_title: When Life Gives You BC, Make Q-functions: Extracting Q-values from Behavior Cloning for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Lakshita Dodeja, Ondrej Biza, Shivam Vats, Stephen Hart, Stefanie Tellex
